functionalObligations.text: A user deposits ETH into the LiquidityPool and receives eETH, recorded as a share of a ledger holding totalShares and shares[address] at a SHARE_UNIT of 1e18; the pool tracks value in two halves, totalValueInLp and totalValueOutOfLp.
functionalObligations.note: The repository is untagged, so the commit hash is the only pin available; b4a0968 is dated 2026-07-15. Bytecode-level correspondence between the deployed upgradeable implementations and this commit is UNKNOWN.

functionalObligations.text: An eETH holder's nominal balance changes when the pool's total value changes, without a transfer.
A single rebase may not raise the pool's total value by more than a hard cap expressed in basis points.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. This is an oracle-error containment device applied to the accounting itself rather than to the oracle: it bounds how far one report may move the ledger, whatever the report says. Gp names a pause and Ex's L13 warrant names freshness validation; neither names a ceiling on the rate of change of a claim's value.

functionalObligations.text: weETH is the non-rebasing wrapper over eETH shares and is the form every integration and every cross-chain deployment uses.
functionalObligations.note: Ix is ADDED on this obligation. Same structure as Lido's wstETH: the wrapper is the adapter that discharges prohibition X4 (Rb into a balance-invariant ledger with no adapter).

functionalObligations.text: A committee of members submits reports keyed by a report hash; once the committee's quorum size is reached the report is published, and an admin contract consumes it, with report periods and reference slots gating when a report is needed and when the previous one must have been handled.
functionalObligations.note: Ex is FORCED and retained, for the same reason as Lido: this is a quorum-signed report of protocol state, not a price feed, and the failure mode is collusion on a balance. Three protocols in this category run this shape and none of them reports a price; that is the category-level finding on Ex.

functionalObligations.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: registration and vetting] A node operator must be registered and whitelisted in NodeOperatorManager, which holds its key data, and carries approval tags mapping it to the categories of pool funds (SourceOfFunds) it is permitted to serve.
functionalObligations.note: Aw is ADDED to the corpus construction, which carries no permission symbol for ether.fi at all. Aw names the admission gate; it does not name the per-source-of-funds scoping, which partitions one operator set into sub-populations serving different pools of capital.

functionalObligations.text: Node operators do not self-select: they bid on chain for the right to be assigned a validator, with bids bounded below and above by minBidAmount and maxBidAmount and a distinct whitelistBidAmount for whitelisted bidders, and the winning bid's revenue is forwarded to the treasury.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the clearest single gap in this protocol. A priced, cleared, on-chain primary market for the operator slot is not an emission, not a fee and not a permission gate; it is closest to a primary auction for a licence. Ba (batch-auction clearing) is deliberately not used: what clears is not a trade at a uniform price but an assignment of a right, and there is no batch.

functionalObligations.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: allocation and scheduling] Only addresses in the validatorSpawner mapping may create validators; creation binds an accepted bid to a newly deployed EtherFiNode beacon proxy and is tracked by a validator-creation status keyed on a hash.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE recorded alongside a used symbol. Aw names the spawner allowlist. What has no symbol is that allocation of principal to operators here is determined by an auction outcome plus an allowlist rather than by a scheduling rule: there is no least-allocated-first policy and no per-operator cap analogous to Lido's stake share limit. Two protocols in this category solve the same allocation problem with structurally incompatible mechanisms and the vocabulary names neither.

functionalObligations.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5: deposit front-running defence] A 1 ETH INITIAL_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT is deposited first, pinning the validator's withdrawal credentials to the EtherFiNode contract, before the remaining balance is committed; validators range from MIN_VALIDATOR_SIZE_WEI of 32 ETH to MAX_VALIDATOR_SIZE_WEI of 2048 ETH.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the third structurally different implementation of the same defence in this category: Lido answers it with a guardian signature quorum, Lido V3 with a predeposit plus an EIP-4788 credential proof and a forfeitable guarantee, ether.fi with a bare 1 ETH predeposit and no proof and no bond. The problem is category-universal and the three answers share no structure, which makes this the strongest candidate in the lane for a new element.

functionalObligations.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit signalling] Exit and consolidation requests are issued from EtherFiNodesManager against a validator pubkey hash, with FULL_EXIT_GWEI of 2,048,000,000,000, and each of unrestaking, exit requests and consolidation requests is metered by its own named rate-limit identifier.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Wq names the user's queue (F13, F14, F15); nothing names the validator-side exit that must complete before those queues can be paid, and nothing names its metering. Any '32 ETH unit' framing of this protocol is stale: it is on Pectra-era 0x02 validators with consolidation, matching Lido's LIP-35 move.

functionalObligations.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5: penalty attribution] A consensus-layer or restaking loss reaches eETH holders as a smaller rebase, with no operator-posted first-loss capital between the operator and the holder: permissioned operators are required to bid but are not required to post a bond as collateral, and solo stakers run without posting any collateral.
functionalObligations.note: TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) Tr is DROPPED. The T-NFT/B-NFT two-tier structure the corpus describes as 'a bond, described in tranche language' is not part of the live system: TNFT.sol and BNFT.sol are in src/archive/, retained only for storage-layout continuity. Any decomposition carrying Tr for ether.fi decomposes a dead mechanism. (2) Bs is DROPPED. With B-NFT archived and the whitepaper stating operators post no bond, stage 1 could identify no operator-posted first-loss capital in the current design; UNKNOWN whether any exists. Sl therefore does the whole of the loss work here, and the absence of any junior layer beneath eETH holders is the finding.

functionalObligations.text: Staking rewards are split 90% to stakers, 5% to node operators and 5% to the protocol, and restaking rewards route separately through a rewards router and a cumulative-Merkle distributor.
functionalObligations.note: Fd is a CANDIDATE symbol, used with the required mark, and is ADDED; Em is DROPPED. Em names protocol-funded emissions of an existing asset; what is distributed here is received reward value, not newly funded incentive. See F19 for what Em was standing in for.

functionalObligations.text: Standard exit: a holder burns eETH for an ERC-721 withdrawal request; an admin finalises a batch, and the claim rate is snapshotted at finalisation with ceiling rounding so that for any finalised token the claimable amount is invariant under subsequent rebases.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE recorded alongside a used symbol, and the contract states this as its own invariant I3, property-tested, headed as 'the H-02 fix' from an audit. Rate freezing at finalisation is a deliberate severing of a claim from the accounting index at a named block: Rb and Wq together cannot say it, because it is the difference between a queue position and a fixed-price forward. Ft (fixed-term debt) is deliberately not used: there is no maturity date, only a frozen price.

functionalObligations.text: Instant exit: a holder redeems eETH or weETH for ETH or stETH immediately in exchange for an exit fee, capped by a refilling token bucket over a time period and floored by a low-watermark expressed in basis points of pool TVL, with a stale-price window and a maximum price threshold on the stETH price feed.
functionalObligations.note: Rd is ADDED: this door is a genuine direct redemption right, priced and capped. Ex is claimed here in its ordinary sense for once, because the stETH price feed is a real price oracle with a freshness bound, which satisfies law L13 and is a different object from the state-reporting committee of F5. The token bucket is RESIDUE; see F16.

functionalObligations.text: Priority exit: whitelisted addresses redeem through a separate queue with an immutable minimum delay, for amounts between 0.01 and 1000 ETH, against a separately locked ETH balance.
functionalObligations.note: Audited only in 2026-03, after the corpus record was written.

functionalObligations.text: The choice among three exit doors, differently priced and carrying different rights, is itself a mechanism: instant is fee-bearing and bucket-limited, standard is free and rate-frozen at an admin's finalisation, priority is whitelisted and delay-bounded.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Wq names one queue. The corpus knows one withdrawal queue for ether.fi; the live protocol has three, and the routing between them determines the price a holder pays to leave. Nothing names a menu of exits with different terms over one claim.

functionalObligations.text: A refilling token-bucket budget meters unrestaking, exit requests, consolidation requests and instant redemptions.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and category-recurrent. This is not a pause and not a cap: it is a refilling budget on a state transition, and it appears four times in this one protocol and in three of the five protocols in this category (here, WBETH's exchange-rate allowance, Lido's per-module deposit rate limits and vault quarantine). Nothing in the 58 names it.

functionalObligations.text: [What the restaked collateral secures] The same principal that backs eETH is natively restaked: the EtherFiNode holding the validators' withdrawal credentials is also an EigenPod, so one deposit serves Ethereum consensus and EigenLayer without a second user action and without a second lockup.
functionalObligations.note: Rs is a CANDIDATE, used with the mark, and is exact in name and thin in content. It asserts restaking is a fact and stops.

functionalObligations.text: [Who may write a slashing condition over the restaked collateral] Neither ether.fi's contracts nor the eETH holder: AVS selection and registration live outside this repository, in etherfi-avs-operator, and the README states restaking and AVS management are strictly controlled by the Protocol.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the thinnest point in the carrier for this application. The party bearing the loss neither chooses nor can observe on chain who is empowered to author the slashing conditions over its principal; the control object is out-of-repo and permissioned. UNKNOWN which AVSs and which restaking venues are live as of 2026-08. Restaking rewards additionally route through KING, a separate protocol organisation, since 2026.

functionalObligations.text: [Whether the same collateral can be committed twice] Yes: the same principal is committed to Ethereum consensus and to EigenLayer operator sets at once. Within EigenLayer the second commitment is bounded, because an operator's magnitude allocations cannot exceed its total magnitude; across venues nothing in ether.fi bounds or discloses the aggregate exposure.
functionalObligations.note: CORRECTION. The corpus residue entry describes restaking 'into several heterogeneous security markets at once (EigenLayer, Symbiotic, Karak) with slashing conditions written by parties who do not know about each other'. Within EigenLayer that is refuted by Unique Stake. Across venues it is not refuted, but stage 1 found no first-party evidence that ether.fi currently restakes anywhere other than EigenLayer: EtherFiRestaker imports only EigenLayer's StrategyManager, DelegationManager and RewardsCoordinator. The multi-venue framing is therefore UNKNOWN rather than established, and stage 2 does not inherit it.

functionalObligations.text: A node contract may execute a bounded set of arbitrary calls into its own EigenPod or into a named external target, gated per caller, per function selector and per target address.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the closest thing in this whole category to Au. Au is deliberately not used: law L17 asks delegated execution scope for bounded scope, revocation, expiry and nonce/domain separation, and only the first two are present. More decisively, the authority is delegated by the protocol to itself, mediated by a role registry, and its purpose is to let one protocol drive another protocol's state machine. Nothing names an adapter with a selector allowlist for driving a foreign protocol.

functionalObligations.text: A protocol-wide blacklister is wired into eETH, the LiquidityPool, the AuctionManager, both withdrawal queues and the redemption manager.
functionalObligations.note: Fz is a CANDIDATE, used with the required mark, and is ADDED: the corpus element list for ether.fi contains no freeze or permission symbol at all. Law L28 asks Fz for a named authority, enumerated triggers, an appeal path and holder disclosure; stage 1 found the authority (RoleRegistry) but not the triggers, the appeal path or the disclosure, so the warrant is partly unmet.

functionalObligations.text: Authority for the whole protocol is centralised in one RoleRegistry contract read by nearly every other contract through a shared mixin; two timelocks are deployed, an upgrade timelock and an operating timelock; every contract is UUPS- or beacon-upgradeable; and a mixin provides time-bounded rather than indefinite pauses.
functionalObligations.note: Law L15 (Up requires Tg or a bounded emergency process) is satisfied twice over, by the upgrade timelock and by the time-bounded pause. RESIDUE recorded here: Tg, Up and Gp describe three separate control mechanisms and cannot express that one registry contract is the authority for all of them, which makes the registry a single point of governance failure that the triple conceals rather than reveals.

functionalObligations.text: Deposits were acquired through an off-chain loyalty-points programme whose balances were later converted into a token.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the reason Em is dropped rather than merely unused. Em names emissions of an existing asset on a published schedule; points are a discretionary, revocable, off-chain promissory ledger with no on-chain representation and no commitment. The on-chain residue of the early programme (EarlyAdopterPool, LoyaltyPointsMarketSafe, membership/) now sits in src/archive/, which is itself the evidence: the instrument lived and died off-ledger, and the vocabulary never saw it.

functionalObligations.text: Some validators are operated as distributed validators, one key split into keyshares across a cluster with a signing threshold, in the solo-staker programme.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The vocabulary has zero coverage of a threshold-signed distributed validator key. The scope claim is NARROWED from the corpus: stage 1 could place Obol/Charon only in the Operation Solo Staker programme, not demonstrably in the main permissioned operator set, and the primary page returned 404 on direct fetch so the 3/4 cluster threshold is UNCONFIRMED at first-party source. UNKNOWN what fraction of ether.fi's validator set is distributed. The category-level point that DVT is the largest unnamed mechanism by TVL stands on Lido's Simple DVT module plus SSV and Obol independently of this entry.

paper.title: ether.fi
paper.label: cat:lsd:etherfi
paper.blurb: A user deposits ETH into the liquidity pool and receives eETH, a share of a ledger whose nominal balance moves with the pool's reported value; weETH is the non-rebasing wrapper, and it is the form every integration and every cross-chain deployment holds. The same principal is staked and restaked at once, because the node contract holding the validators' withdrawal credentials is itself a pod; which services that stake secures, and therefore who is empowered to author the conditions under which it is destroyed, is settled by the protocol in contracts outside this repository. Operators do not select themselves: they bid on chain for the right to be assigned a validator, and the winning bid is forwarded to the treasury. Exit is a choice among doors --- instant for a fee, metered by a refilling bucket and floored on pool value; a standard queue whose claim rate is frozen at an administrator's finalisation and thereafter invariant under rebases; and a priority queue for whitelisted addresses under a minimum delay. Nothing sits beneath the holder: operators post no bond, so a consensus-layer or restaking loss reaches eETH as a smaller rebase and stops there.
paper.witnessReason: The tranche element is dropped: the tiered note structure the corpus record describes as a bond in tranche language now sits in the repository's archive directory, retained for storage-layout continuity, so a decomposition carrying it decomposes a dead mechanism. The bond element goes with it, because the whitepaper states that permissioned operators are required to bid and not to post collateral and that solo stakers post none either, and no other first-loss layer could be identified --- which leaves loss allocation doing the whole of the work, and the absence of any junior layer beneath the holder as the result. A permission element, a freeze element, a direct-redemption element and an index element are all added, because the record carries no access or freeze symbol for this protocol at all, the instant door is a genuine priced redemption right, and the wrapper is the adapter that keeps a rebasing claim admissible in balance-invariant ledgers. The record's multi-venue restaking framing is not inherited: within a single venue it is refuted by that venue's conserved allocation budget, and across venues the restaking contract imports the interfaces of one venue only, so the framing is unknown rather than established.
paper.residueNote: The protocol's own file layout is the argument: registration, the market for the slot, the key and predeposit path, exit and consolidation, and the restaking leg are separate contracts, and the candidate symbol for this category would collapse every one of them into itself. The market is the sharpest --- a priced, cleared, on-chain primary auction for the right to operate is not an emission, not a fee and not a permission gate, and nothing names it. Beneath it sit a refilling budget metering a state transition, which recurs across this category and has no symbol; a claim severed from the accounting index at a named block, which is the difference between a queue position and a fixed-price forward; and a menu of exits over one claim, where the routing is itself the price of leaving. The same principal is committed to consensus and to an external security market at once: within that market a conserved budget bounds the second commitment, and across markets nothing here bounds it or discloses the aggregate. The party that bears the loss neither chooses nor can observe on chain who may write the conditions under which its principal is destroyed, and that is the thinnest point in the carrier for this application.
